ops.new_text:
\title{\rev{A chance-corrected benchmark of ECG representations for unsupervised
arrhythmia structure}}

ops.rationale: The abstract defines the ceiling and feature scaling, ties the above-chance ceiling to the conv-AE only, gives the scaling and stressor results by their measures, names ECGFounder and the conv-AE, states the contribution without the ranking shape and cuts the unhedged closing sentence.
ops.new_text:
\begin{abstract}
Unsupervised analysis of the electrocardiogram (ECG) promises label-free
discovery of cardiac structure, yet whether clustering succeeds depends less on
the algorithm than on how the signal is represented. We benchmark four
representation families for unsupervised separation of sinus rhythm (SR) from
atrial fibrillation (AF) on PTB-XL: \rev{whole-record} raw flattening, a convolutional
\rev{autoencoder (conv-AE)}, compact hand-crafted rhythm and morphology features,
and two frozen foundation-model embeddings (HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder).
Evaluation is chance-corrected (adjusted Rand index, ARI), patient-grouped,
\rev{repeated over ten seeds for the clusterers that depend on one}, and bounded by a
supervised ceiling\rev{, the accuracy a supervised probe reaches on the same features}. ECGFounder clusters
best (ARI up to 0.885), but 16 interpretable hand-crafted features are competitive
(0.711) and far ahead of the raw and \rev{conv-AE} pipelines (ARI $\approx 0$)\rev{.
Both match a majority-class assignment, the conv-AE despite a supervised ceiling of 0.678
and the raw pipeline with a ceiling of 0.519 against a majority of 0.504.}
The same ordering holds on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task. Two cautions emerge: the
silhouette score rewards the degenerate one-cluster solution (silhouette 0.81 at
ARI \rev{0.000}) and cannot validate ECG clustering alone, and \rev{feature scaling, the
per-feature transformation applied before clustering, moves the mean ARI of the
hand-crafted features from 0.229 to 0.629 across four scalers.
The chance-corrected controls locate where naive pipelines fail.
Under heavy class imbalance, at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio, the hand-crafted features keep the
highest ARI and overtake ECGFounder.
Under federation across ten sites that differ in class prevalence they retain the largest
share of their centralized ARI, 0.92 against 0.69 for ECGFounder, at about one fifteenth
of its inference time per record.}
\end{abstract}

ops.rationale: Joins the first two Introduction paragraphs, opens on the point, drops the unsupported claims about most ECG work and the usual attribution, names the specific questions, uses record for one ECG, glosses purity and the silhouette, cuts simply and describes the master's project as unpublished in place of a citation.
ops.new_text:
\rev{On the two arrhythmia tasks this study evaluates, whether clustering of the
electrocardiogram (ECG) recovers a clinical label depends on the representation fed to
the clustering algorithm and on how the result is evaluated.
Some clinical questions are unsupervised: which patients group together, what subtypes
exist, and whether structure can be found without labels that are expensive or
unavailable.
A natural first attempt is to cluster the records directly.
This study began as a re-examination of an unpublished master's project that did so.
That project flattened each 12-lead record into a long vector, compressed it with a dense
autoencoder, and clustered the code.
It reported high cluster purity, the share of the majority class inside each cluster, and
a silhouette score near 0.89, the silhouette being a label-free index of cluster
compactness.
Neither number measured agreement with the classes: the purity equalled the
majority-class proportion in every setting, and the silhouette was measured on a
degenerate solution in which almost all records fell into a single cluster.
The project's conclusion, that the difficulty lies in processing the raw signal rather
than in the clustering step, is correct, and this study makes it precise.}

Joins the short paragraph on the closest benchmark to the paragraph on the gap, and replaces the self-assessment and the unsupported default and canonical claims with the two additions and their held citations.
ops.new_text:
A representation can carry information about a label and still fail to cluster by it.
Linear separability and clusterability are distinct properties: a representation may
place the discriminative direction far from its dominant axes of variation, so that a
supervised probe recovers the label while an unsupervised partition does not. This
distinction is established in the self-supervised learning literature
\cite{sslclustering2025}, and we treat it as background rather than as a finding. What
has not been measured, for ECG, is how the common representation families compare on
this axis under proper chance-corrected metrics.
The most directly related work benchmarks several ECG foundation models against one
another, including a cluster-separability analysis on PTB-XL \cite{lookingbeyond2026}.
By its own statement it does not include a representation-wise comparison against
hand-crafted features, and it omits the MIT-BIH database.
\rev{This study adds both: a hand-crafted arm built from RR-interval and beat-morphology
features \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, and a beat-morphology task on the MIT-BIH
Arrhythmia Database \cite{mitbih2001}.}

Keeps the one statement that the ordering is expected, sets the four contributions as a list, defines patient-grouped, the ceiling, internal indices and feature scaling, names the conv-AE and the non-IID sites, gives the stressor result by its measures and words the model scope once.
ops.new_text:
We therefore benchmark four representation families for unsupervised SR-versus-AF
separation \rev{(sinus rhythm versus atrial fibrillation)}, with the controls the original
pipeline lacked. \rev{Because SR and AF differ by definition in the regularity of the
rhythm, it is expected that compact hand-crafted features and a large foundation model
both recover the split.
The ordering of the representations is therefore not the contribution.
What the benchmark adds is what the controls reveal and how the representations behave
under deployment stress.} Our contributions are modest and empirical\rev{:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] A chance-corrected, patient-grouped and significance-tested clustering
benchmark of raw, convolutional autoencoder (conv-AE), hand-crafted, and two frozen
foundation-model representations. Patient-grouped means that no patient appears in more
than one fold. Each representation is bounded by a supervised ceiling, the accuracy a
supervised probe reaches on the same features, and the comparison is shown stable across
the assumed number of clusters.
\item[(ii)] Two reproducible methodological cautions that explain the original project's
misleading numbers. Internal validity indices such as the silhouette, which are computed
without labels, reward the degenerate collapse. Feature scaling, the per-feature
transformation applied to a representation before clustering (Yeo-Johnson power,
standard, quantile or robust scaling), changes the result by a wide margin.
\item[(iii)] The behaviour of the representations under two independent deployment
stressors: heavy class imbalance, and federation across sites that differ in class
proportions (non-IID). The 16 hand-crafted features keep the highest adjusted Rand index
(ARI) at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio and the largest share of their centralized ARI under non-IID
federation.
\item[(iv)] A generalization check on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task, the dataset the
closest prior benchmark omits.
\end{enumerate}
\end{revblock}
We do not propose a new method. \rev{The statements about foundation models concern
HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder, the two evaluated here, and the
separability-versus-clusterability phenomenon is credited to prior work.}

ops.rationale: Replaces the unsupported autoencoder claim with what the objective holds by definition, says what the undefined spectrum phrase means, and splits the sentence at the semicolon.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Unsupervised ECG and representations.} Hand-crafted features built from
RR-interval irregularity and beat morphology encode the defining signatures of common
arrhythmias and underpin decades of automatic analysis \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}.
Tensor and wavelet decompositions have been combined with spectral clustering for
unsupervised 12-lead classification \cite{wavelettensorecg2018}. \rev{A reconstruction
autoencoder is trained to reproduce its input and receives no class information, so
nothing in its objective arranges its code by class.} Contrastive self-supervised
methods built on physiologically motivated augmentations and patient- or lead-level
invariances, including CLOCS \cite{clocs2021}, 3KG \cite{threekg2021}, and contrastive
predictive coding for 12-lead ECG \cite{mehari2022ssl}, established the pretraining
recipes that later foundation models scaled up. Self-supervised and foundation models for
ECG, such as HuBERT-ECG \cite{hubertecg2024} and ECGFounder \cite{ecgfounder2024}, learn
general representations from millions of recordings and are now evaluated as frozen
feature extractors. The wavelet-tensor and spectral-clustering pipeline of
\cite{wavelettensorecg2018} addresses a related unsupervised goal with a different
(tensor) representation\rev{. This study focuses on four families, which range from
representations shaped only by signal energy, raw flattening and a reconstruction
autoencoder, to features built from the defining signatures of the classes, and include
two frozen foundation embeddings. A tensor arm is left to future work.}

ops.rationale: Replaces near zero with the exact values of ARI and AMI for the one-cluster solution and under random assignment.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Clustering evaluation.} Cluster purity is not chance-corrected: assigning
every point to the majority class attains a purity equal to that class's prevalence.
External, chance-corrected indices, the adjusted Rand index \cite{hubertarabie1985} and
adjusted mutual information \cite{vinh2010}, \rev{are exactly zero for the one-cluster
solution, have expected value zero under random assignment,}
and are the appropriate headline metrics. Internal indices such as the silhouette
\cite{rousseeuw1987} measure compactness in the embedding being clustered and can be
maximised by degenerate solutions, so they require cluster-size sanity checks.

ops.rationale: Reports the closest benchmark's results in the past tense, splits the sentence at the semicolon and avoids repeating the both-gaps statement of the Introduction.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Closest benchmark.} \rev{The ECG foundation-model benchmark of
\cite{lookingbeyond2026} reported cluster-separability (ARI) of foundation-model
embeddings on PTB-XL and found that some models clustered by clinical label while others
clustered by dataset. It compared foundation models to one another and stated that prior
work omits a representation-wise evaluation. It did not add a hand-crafted baseline, and
it did not include MIT-BIH. Beyond these two additions, this study adds a supervised
ceiling so that a low clustering score can be attributed to geometry rather than to
missing information.}

ops.rationale: Past tense for the method, expands AFIB and AFLT and says both count as AF, states the input in the field's terms without the function name and data-type identifier, rewords the load-time phrase and removes the two semicolons.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{PTB-XL.} \rev{We used PTB-XL \cite{ptbxl2020}, a public 12-lead database of
21\,799 records from 18\,869 patients, each record 10\,s long. Rhythm labels were taken
from the SCP-ECG (Standard Communications Protocol for Computer-Assisted
Electrocardiography) statements. The SR-versus-AF cohort used as positives all records
carrying an AF statement, atrial fibrillation (AFIB) or atrial flutter (AFLT), so that both
count as AF, and as controls the sinus-rhythm records without any AF statement.}
PTB-XL encodes rhythm statements at a likelihood of zero meaning ``present'',
\rev{so a presence-based rule was required, since a confidence threshold would have
discarded every SR record. We drew} a balanced, patient-disjoint cohort of 2\,542 records
(1\,282 SR, 1\,260 AF), so the majority-class baseline is 0.504. \rev{Records were read
from the WFDB-format files of the \mbox{100\,Hz} release of the database and converted once
to a single-precision floating-point array of 1000 samples by 12 leads. No filtering,
resampling or rescaling was applied before each representation's own preprocessing, so
every representation started from the same array. The lead set and any further
preprocessing were chosen per representation rather than once for the whole study, and
are stated with each representation below.} All evaluation \rev{was} patient-grouped: no
patient appears in more than one fold or in both classes.

ops.rationale: Develops the short MIT-BIH paragraph with the cohort details main.tex already holds (window dimension, grouping, how the task differs, the three clusterers), in the past tense.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{MIT-BIH.} \rev{For generalization we used} the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database
\cite{mitbih2001,physionet2000}. \rev{Each annotated beat was segmented into a window of
$[-300, +250]$\,ms around the R-peak across both leads, which gives the raw beat window
about 400 dimensions (Table~\ref{tab:mitbih}). We formed a balanced
normal-versus-premature-ventricular (N-vs-V) task of 3\,000 beats (1\,500 per class) from
47 records, with the record as the grouping unit, so that no record contributes beats to
more than one fold.} This is a morphology task and a deliberate contrast to the PTB-XL
rhythm task\rev{: the PTB-XL classes differ in the timing of the beats across a 10\,s
record, whereas the two MIT-BIH classes are defined on single beats and differ in beat
morphology. The MIT-BIH beats were clustered with the $k$-means, Ward agglomerative and
Gaussian-mixture clusterers described below.}

ops.rationale: Cuts the announcing sentence and introduces the list with a colon, drops the data-type identifiers, rewrites the four principle sentences by content, splits the lead-set and lead II sentences, words the MIT-BIH carry-over as feature logic, marks the missing definition of beat-template consistency, uses record for one ECG and moves the MIT-BIH paragraph into the lead-set paragraph of OP014.
ops.new_text:
We compare four families on PTB-XL (Table~\ref{tab:main})\rev{:}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Raw flattening} reproduces the original pipeline: each lead \rev{was}
moving-average downsampled and all leads \rev{were} concatenated into one vector
($\sim$2000 dimensions). It carries amplitude and energy but no \rev{cross-record}
temporal alignment. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, 1000 samples by 12 leads. A
non-overlapping six-sample mean per lead left 166 samples per lead and a
1992-dimensional vector. This arm treats the sample amplitudes as the features and
imposes no clinical model on the signal. All twelve leads entered because the arm
reproduces the originating pipeline, which concatenated every lead.}
\item \textbf{Convolutional autoencoder} (conv-AE): a 1-D convolutional autoencoder
with a 32-unit bottleneck, trained to convergence with a validation split. This is a
properly specified reconstruction model, in contrast to the original collapsed dense
autoencoder. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, resampled to 12 by 2500 and z-scored per lead.
A reconstruction objective compresses whatever carries signal energy, which need not be
what separates the classes.}
\item \textbf{Hand-crafted} (16 features): RR-interval statistics and irregularity
\rev{(the standard deviation of the RR intervals (SDNN), the root mean square of successive
RR differences (RMSSD), the proportion of successive RR differences above \mbox{50\,ms}
(pNN50), the coefficient of variation, RR entropy and mean heart rate)}, P-wave
presence and amplitude, QRS width and amplitude, and beat-template consistency\rev{,
[GAP: one-clause definition of beat-template consistency, from the study's feature
extraction]} \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, extracted with NeuroKit2
\cite{neurokit2021}. \rev{Input: lead II alone, 1000 samples, reduced to a
16-dimensional single-precision vector. R-peak detection and wave delineation were
performed on that one lead. Lead II is the standard rhythm lead, on which RR regularity
and P-wave presence are read. Single-lead recordings are the established setting for
automated AF detection \cite{clifford2017af}. A single-lead definition also lets the
feature logic, RR timing and beat morphology, be carried to the two-lead MIT-BIH beats as
the 21-dimensional beat-morphology set, where a twelve-lead definition would not apply.
The arm measures directly the AF signature, RR irregularity together with P-wave
absence.}
\item \textbf{Foundation embeddings} (frozen): mean-pooled hidden states of HuBERT-ECG
(768-d) \cite{hubertecg2024} and the 1024-d pooled features of ECGFounder
\cite{ecgfounder2024}, both used as fixed feature extractors with no fine-tuning.
\rev{Input: all twelve leads. HuBERT-ECG received the first \mbox{5\,s} at
\mbox{100\,Hz}, flattened lead-major into a 6000-sample vector. ECGFounder received the
full \mbox{10\,s} record resampled to 12 by 5000 for its \mbox{500\,Hz} input and
z-scored once over the whole array. Both lead sets are fixed by the published models,
which are defined on the complete twelve-lead record. The pretrained models supply a
fixed ECG feature space, and the question is whether that space places the rhythm
classes in separate regions.}
\end{itemize}

ops.rationale: Joins the two short lead-set paragraphs, keeps the one statement of the 12-lead constraint, words the MIT-BIH carry-over as feature logic, hedges the lead-set reading with the 1992-dimensional alternative and removes the semicolons.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The arms use different lead sets, and each choice answers a different constraint.
The hand-crafted arm is single-lead by clinical convention and so that its feature logic
carries to the two-lead MIT-BIH beats. The raw arm is twelve-lead because that is the
pipeline it reproduces. The raw arm therefore receives more input than the hand-crafted
arm, so missing input does not explain its chance-level clustering. The twelve-lead input
also makes the raw vector 1992-dimensional, which may itself weaken Euclidean clustering.
On MIT-BIH the PTB-XL rhythm features do not carry over to single beats, so the
comparison there is between a raw beat window, a 21-dimensional beat-morphology and
RR-context feature set, and the conv-AE. The two foundation models were not applied to
the 2-lead beats, because both are tied to the 12-lead input format.}

ops.rationale: Splits the 583-word paragraph by idea in the past tense, sets the clusterer settings and the metric notation as lists, uses feature scaling and scaler throughout, rewords the evaluation-mode phrase and removes the semicolons.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each representation was clustered with five algorithms as implemented in scikit-learn
\cite{sklearn2011}, with the number of clusters set to the number of classes:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item $k$-means, with ten restarts per seed.
\item Ward agglomerative clustering, with Ward linkage on Euclidean distance.
\item Spectral clustering, with a nearest-neighbour affinity and $k$-means label
assignment.
\item A Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with diagonal covariance and a covariance floor of
\mbox{$10^{-4}$}, since a full covariance is singular for the high-dimensional
representations.
\item Hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN)
\cite{hdbscan2013}, with a minimum cluster size of $n/50$ rounded down and floored at 10,
with $n$ the number of records. On the PTB-XL cohort this is 50 records.
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}
\rev{Tolerances and iteration caps were the library defaults, and no early stopping was
imposed on the clusterers. Ward agglomerative clustering and HDBSCAN are deterministic
given the input matrix, so each was fitted once rather than once per seed.}

\rev{The conv-AE was trained with Adam at a learning rate of \mbox{$10^{-3}$}, batch size
64, for at most 50 epochs on a 90/10 train/validation split. Training stopped when the
validation reconstruction error had not improved for eight epochs, and the
best-validation weights were restored. The two foundation models were applied with their
published weights frozen. HuBERT-ECG was mean-pooled over time from its last hidden layer
at batch size 64, and ECGFounder returned its globally average-pooled 1024-dimensional
feature layer at batch size 32.}

\rev{The headline metrics were the chance-corrected adjusted Rand index (ARI)
\cite{hubertarabie1985} and adjusted mutual information (AMI) \cite{vinh2010}.
Normalized mutual information (NMI), V-measure, Fowlkes-Mallows, purity, silhouette
\cite{rousseeuw1987}, and the largest-cluster fraction were reported alongside. Every
metric was computed against a majority and a random baseline. Table~\ref{tab:metrics}
gives each reported metric with its definition, its range, and how a value on it is read,
in this notation:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item $U$ is the partition by true class and $V$ the partition by cluster.
\item $n$ is the number of records and $n_{ij}$ the number of records in class $i$ and
cluster $j$.
\item RI is the fraction of record pairs on which $U$ and $V$ agree.
\item $I$ and $H$ are mutual information and entropy, with $\bar{H}$ the arithmetic mean
of $H(U)$ and $H(V)$.
\item $E[\cdot]$ is the expectation under the permutation model that holds both sets of
group sizes fixed.
\item $a_k$ and $b_k$ are the mean distance from record $k$ to the rest of its own
cluster and to the nearest other cluster.
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}
\rev{None of the eight metrics carries a physical unit. The first five are dimensionless
indices of agreement between the true partition and the recovered one, purity is the
majority-class share inside the clusters, the silhouette is a dimensionless index of
cluster compactness computed without labels, and the largest-cluster fraction is a
proportion of the cohort.}

\rev{A supervised ceiling bounds how much of the label a probe recovers from the same
features under the same patient-grouped five-fold protocol. We report both a linear probe
(balanced logistic regression) and a non-linear probe (random forest), so that a high
ceiling with a low ARI identifies a geometric rather than an informational failure. Each
configuration was repeated over ten seeds, and the headline contrasts were tested with a
paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across seeds.}

\rev{Because heavy-tailed features can dominate Euclidean distance, we swept four scalers
for feature scaling (Yeo-Johnson power, standard, quantile and robust) and report power
scaling as the default unless stated otherwise. Each scaler was fitted on the full
representation matrix, and any hand-crafted feature a record left undefined was filled
with that feature's cohort median before scaling. To check that fixing the cluster count
to the number of classes does not flatter the comparison, we also report adjusted mutual
information, which is comparable across cluster counts, for $K$ from 2 to 8. Because the
natural SR-to-AF prevalence is imbalanced, we additionally evaluated on a 9:1 SR:AF
subsample.}

ops.rationale: Puts the description of how the metrics treated the HDBSCAN noise label in the past tense, matching the rest of Section 3.3.
ops.new_text:
\rev{HDBSCAN labels records it does not assign to any dense region as noise, and the
metrics treated that label in two ways. ARI, AMI, NMI, V-measure and Fowlkes-Mallows
received the prediction unchanged, so the noise records formed one further group of their
own and were charged against the agreement with the true partition. Purity and the
silhouette were computed on the assigned records only, because neither is defined for a
set that is not a cluster, and the purity denominator stayed the full cohort. Noise
records were never dropped from the evaluation and never reassigned to a nearest cluster.
This is why HDBSCAN sat at the bottom of every representation: at this minimum cluster
size it assigned a minority of the cohort on the representations that cluster well, and
on the raw, conv-AE and HuBERT-ECG matrices it labelled the entire cohort as noise, which
left one group and an ARI of exactly zero.}

ops.rationale: Names the interval the patient-grouped bootstrap, states that holding the partitions fixed leaves out the variation of refitting the clustering, and puts the procedure in the past tense.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Uncertainty was quantified at two levels, which answer different questions. A
percentile bootstrap over the ten per-seed values, \mbox{10\,000} resamples, measures how
far a result moves when only the random seed moves. These intervals were narrow: across
the five PTB-XL representations the $k$-means seed interval spans less than 0.002 in ARI,
and for two of them it has zero width because every seed returns the same partition. Ward
agglomerative and HDBSCAN have no seed interval at all, since each is fitted once. A seed
interval therefore carries no more information than the seed standard deviation it would
replace. The interval reported with the results is the second one, the patient-grouped
bootstrap, a percentile bootstrap over the evaluation cohort with \mbox{5\,000}
resamples. It holds the partitions fixed and resamples the cohort with replacement at the
patient level, so every record of a drawn patient travels with it. Because the partitions
are held fixed, these intervals do not include the variation that refitting the
clustering on each resample would add. The statistic resampled is the quantity the tables
report, the mean ARI over the ten seeds where the clusterer is seeded and the single fit
where it is not, so each interval contains its own point estimate. All intervals are the
2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap distribution at a fixed bootstrap seed.}

ops.rationale: Past tense for what was reported, keeping the one explanation of the p-value floor that the Results now refer to.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was reported with two effect sizes. With ten
paired seeds the two-sided p-value is pinned at its floor of 0.002 as soon as every seed
moves the same way, so it separates none of the contrasts and cannot express a magnitude.
Cliff's delta gives the dominance of one arm over the other across all cross-seed pairs, on
a scale from $-1$ to $1$, and the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation rescales the
signed-rank statistic itself onto the same scale. Each headline contrast additionally
carried the paired difference in ARI with its own patient-grouped bootstrap interval.}

ops.rationale: Cuts the repeated no-new-method clause with its semicolon, uses feature scaling, rewords the run sentence as a description of each federated clustering, in the past tense.
ops.new_text:
\rev{To probe deployment under data siloing we used standard federated $k$-means with
FedAvg-style centroid aggregation \cite{fedavg2017}. The 2\,542 records were partitioned,
patient-grouped, across ten simulated sites, either independently and identically
distributed (IID) or with class proportions drawn from a Dirichlet distribution so that
sites differ sharply in arrhythmia prevalence (non-IID). The Dirichlet concentration was
0.3, applied per class over the ten sites, and any site left holding fewer records than
clusters was dropped. Feature scaling was fitted once on the full representation matrix
before partitioning, so the federation concerns the clustering step alone. Each federated
clustering consisted of fifteen aggregation rounds of three local Lloyd iterations per
site, with the server replacing each centroid by the mean of the site centroids weighted
by the number of records each site assigned to it, and the centroids initialised globally
from two randomly drawn records. Both settings were repeated over ten seeds, with the site
partition and the centroid initialisation redrawn at each seed.} We report the
global ARI relative to centralized clustering of the same representation.

ops.rationale: Replaces the sentence heading with a label.
ops.new_text: \subsection[PTB-XL benchmark]{\rev{PTB-XL benchmark}}

ops.rationale: Opens with the point, gives the spreads across representations and across clusterers from Table main that support it, and reports the values in the past tense.
ops.new_text:
\rev{On PTB-XL the representation decided the clustering outcome more than the algorithm
did (Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:heatmap}). Across representations the best
ARI ranged from 0.008 for the conv-AE to 0.885 for ECGFounder. Within each of the two
representations that clustered well, the four clusterers other than HDBSCAN stayed closer
together, from 0.709 to 0.885 for ECGFounder and from 0.544 to 0.711 for the hand-crafted
features, and HDBSCAN, which labels most records as noise, lay below them at 0.137 and
0.060. ECGFounder clustered best (ARI up to 0.885 with $k$-means), the hand-crafted
features were competitive (0.711 with agglomerative clustering), HuBERT-ECG was weak
(0.195), and the raw and conv-AE pipelines were indistinguishable from a majority-class
assignment (ARI $\approx 0$).}

strongly while HuBERT-ECG did not, which matches the report of \cite{lookingbeyond2026}

ops.new_text:
\rev{Each representation's position follows from two things: how much of the label its
space holds, which the supervised ceiling in the last column of Table~\ref{tab:main}
measures, and where in the space that label lies. The hand-crafted representation is
16-dimensional and each coordinate is a quantity by which the classes are defined, RR
irregularity and P-wave presence. Its ceiling was 0.942 and an unsupervised partition
recovered 0.711. ECGFounder had the highest ceiling, 0.983, recovered the most, 0.885,
and led at every $K$ from 2 to 8, so the rhythm split is one of the larger sources of
variation in its 1024 dimensions. HuBERT-ECG had almost the same ceiling as the
hand-crafted features, 0.899, and recovered 0.195.}

\rev{The conv-AE and raw flattening show two different ways for a representation to fail.
The conv-AE ceiling of 0.678 is what a bottleneck optimised to reconstruct signal energy
retains of a class it was never asked about, and it recovered 0.008. Raw flattening
reached 0.519 against a majority of 0.504, so a linear probe found little label
information in the 1992-dimensional vector. A likely reason is that its coordinates are
amplitudes at fixed sample offsets, and no fixed offset falls on the same part of the
cardiac cycle in two records. A random forest on the same vector reached 0.714, so some
label information remains that a linear probe does not reach. Both rows sat at a
majority-class assignment under all five clusterers, the raw vector because it holds
little label information that a linear probe recovers, and the conv-AE code because it
holds more without arranging it into clusters. Changing the clustering algorithm
addresses neither.}

ops.new_text: \subsection[Supervised ceiling and clusterability]{\rev{Supervised ceiling and clusterability}}

ops.rationale: Says the raw pipeline carried little linearly recoverable label information, cuts simply, interprets the random-forest values on the hand-crafted features and ECGFounder, splits the paragraph at the probe test, in the past tense and without the semicolons.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The supervised ceilings (last column of Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:sep})
exposed the gap between separability and clusterability. The raw pipeline carried little
label information that a linear probe recovers (ceiling 0.519, barely above the 0.504
majority), consistent with its chance-level clustering. The conv-AE was more separable
(0.678) yet still clustered at chance (best ARI 0.008, from Ward agglomerative): a
properly trained reconstruction autoencoder encodes the class without organising it into
clusters. HuBERT-ECG was the sharpest case, with a ceiling of 0.899 but an ARI of only
0.195. ECGFounder and the hand-crafted features achieved both high separability and high
clusterability. The discriminative information exists in the weaker embeddings but does
not lie along their dominant axes of variation, the established
separability-versus-clusterability effect \cite{sslclustering2025}.}

\rev{A non-linear probe showed that the gap is not an artefact of a linear one. A random
forest on the raw features reached accuracy 0.714, well above its linear ceiling of 0.519
and far above its clustering ARI of 0.000, so even a non-linear decoder recovers a label
that clustering does not. The same probe gave 0.951 on the hand-crafted features, 0.983 on
ECGFounder and 0.825 on HuBERT-ECG. On the two representations that clustered well it
added little over the linear ceiling, 0.951 against 0.942 for the hand-crafted features
and 0.9835 against 0.9831 for ECGFounder, so their label information is already linearly
accessible. For HuBERT-ECG the random forest sat below the linear ceiling of 0.899, so
probe linearity does not account for that gap either.}

ops.rationale: Opens with the out-of-fold result in place of the cold-open reading, adds the 5 s input window as a possible contributor to HuBERT-ECG's low ARI, splits procedure from interpretation, in the past tense and without the semicolons.
ops.new_text:
\rev{A single discriminant direction estimated from other patients more than tripled
HuBERT-ECG's held-out ARI, so its class information is present and lies off its dominant
axes of variation. In this out-of-fold test, a linear discriminant was fitted on the
training patients of a patient-grouped stratified five-fold split, the held-out patients
were projected onto that single axis, and the projection was clustered with $k$-means
without labels. The comparison arm was $k$-means on the same held-out records in their
native representation. Fitting the discriminant on every label and then clustering the
projection would recover the labels by construction, which is why the projected patients
were held out. Over five folds and ten seeds, on 508 or 509 held-out records per fold, the
mean ARI rose from 0.160 to 0.549 for HuBERT-ECG, from 0.003 to 0.121 for the conv-AE,
from 0.646 to 0.758 for the hand-crafted features and from 0.893 to 0.923 for ECGFounder,
and did not move for raw flattening, 0.000 to 0.001. These are held-out values, so the
native column does not equal the full-cohort $k$-means ARIs of Table~\ref{tab:main}. The
largest difference is 0.013, on HuBERT-ECG.}

\rev{HuBERT-ECG is where the native and projected values separate furthest, and its gain
shows that its class information transfers across patients. HuBERT-ECG also receives only
the first \mbox{5\,s} of each \mbox{10\,s} record, about half the RR intervals the other
arms see, which may contribute to its low native ARI alongside this off-axis reading.
ECGFounder gained almost nothing, because its dominant axes already carry the split. The
conv-AE rose off chance and stopped far short of its ceiling of 0.678, so its class
structure is both off-axis and diffuse. Raw flattening did not move at all, which
separates its failure from HuBERT-ECG's: no single direction estimated from other
patients separates the classes in it, and whatever the non-linear probe recovers from it
is not of that form.}

ops.new_text: \subsection[Internal validity indices]{\rev{Internal validity indices}}

ops.rationale: Opens with the point, replaces a handful with the largest-cluster fraction the text holds, reports in the past tense and shortens the paragraph.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The silhouette, an internal index, rewarded a degenerate solution on this cohort.
Raw flattening with agglomerative clustering attained a silhouette of 0.81 while the
largest cluster held the cohort to two decimals (largest-cluster fraction 1.00) and the
ARI was 0.000. The hand-crafted representation, which recovered the classes (ARI 0.711,
balanced clusters), had a \emph{lower} silhouette of 0.28 (Fig.~\ref{fig:trap}).} A
degenerate one-cluster solution maximises compactness while carrying no class
information. This is the artefact behind the original project's silhouette of 0.89, and it
is why chance-corrected external metrics, read together with cluster-size sanity checks,
are necessary.

ops.new_text:
\rev{Feature scaling changed the outcome by a wide margin. For the hand-crafted features
the mean ARI over clusterers was 0.629 under standard scaling and 0.606 under power
scaling, but fell to 0.360 under robust scaling and 0.229 under quantile scaling. The
effect was not confined to the hand-crafted features: ECGFounder's mean ARI dropped from
0.866 (standard) to 0.093 under robust scaling. Robust scaling leaves heavy arrhythmic
tails unbounded, so that a few outliers dominate Euclidean distance and the partition
collapses. A clustering result on these representations therefore needs its scaler
stated, and this study reports power scaling unless stated otherwise.}

(Table~\ref{tab:mitbih}). On the N-vs-V beat-morphology task the 21-dimensional
beat-morphology features clustered well (ARI 0.783), whereas the raw beat window did not
(ARI 0.018 with $k$-means and 0.049 with agglomerative clustering) despite the beats being

of only 0.127, from the Gaussian mixture. That the same pattern appeared for rhythm on

definitions, supports the representation-level reading.}

ECGFounder fell from 0.885 to 0.612, the hand-crafted features from 0.644 to 0.591 and

ops.new_text:
\rev{For the PTB-XL rhythm task and the MIT-BIH morphology task, the results support a
decision rule.} If a strong public foundation model can be run on balanced data in the
target 12-lead format, ECGFounder gives the best unsupervised separation here. If the data
are imbalanced or siloed across sites, if interpretability or low dimensionality matters,
or if the leads on hand are not the standard twelve, the 16 hand-crafted features are the
better choice: they are within reach of ECGFounder on balanced data\rev{ (0.711 against
0.885), lead it at the 9:1 ratio (0.265 against 0.063) and retain 0.92 of their
centralized ARI under non-IID federation against its 0.69, all on the PTB-XL cohort. The
cost comparison of Table~\ref{tab:cost} points the same way: the representation that held
up better under both stressors is also the lower-cost one to compute. The lead constraint
is concrete. The two foundation models we test could not be applied to the 2-lead MIT-BIH
beats, whereas the hand-crafted feature logic carried to them as the 21-dimensional
beat-morphology set.}

\rev{On PTB-XL the raw and conv-AE pipelines were indistinguishable from a majority-class
assignment under all five clusterers. On MIT-BIH, evaluated with three clusterers, the
conv-AE reached at most 0.127 and the raw beat window at most 0.049, against 0.783 for the
beat-morphology features. On both tasks these two pipelines, including the raw arm that
reproduces the input of the original project's design, recovered far less of the class
structure than the hand-crafted representations.}

Opens with what separates the study from the closest benchmark, sets the six differences as a list of full sentences, cuts the repeated no-novelty statements and the restating close, and uses ordering and feature scaling.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Six elements separate this study from the closest ECG foundation-model clustering
benchmark \cite{lookingbeyond2026}:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item A hand-crafted axis turns a comparison between foundation models into a comparison
between representation families.
\item A supervised ceiling on every representation, linear and non-linear, tells a space
that does not hold the label apart from one that holds it in the wrong geometry.
\item An out-of-fold test of that distinction shows that a discriminant fitted on other
patients raises HuBERT-ECG from 0.160 to 0.549 in held-out ARI.
\item A second dataset and a second task type, the MIT-BIH beat-morphology task, extend
the comparison to the database that benchmark omits.
\item Two cautions a practitioner can act on are stated with their evidence: the
degenerate silhouette, and the dependence of the result on feature scaling.
\item Two deployment stressors are measured with the cost of each representation beside
them, and under these stressors the balanced-data ordering stops being the useful answer.
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}

ops.rationale: Keeps the full scope statement here and gives the two models' best ARIs without calling them the ends of the measured range.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The foundation-model axis is bounded to two models by selection rather than by survey.
HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder both publish weights that load into a frozen feature extractor
without fine-tuning, which is what a benchmark of frozen embeddings requires, and they differ
in pretraining objective and architecture, a self-supervised transformer
\cite{hubertecg2024} against a convolutional model pretrained on more than ten million
recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}. Their best ARIs here are 0.885 and 0.195, so the
foundation arm is not a single point. What the
bound does to the conclusions is to scope them: every statement here about a foundation model
is a statement about one of these two, the deployment comparison is between the hand-crafted
features and ECGFounder specifically, and none of it extends to ECG foundation models as a
class. A further model that clusters as well as ECGFounder on balanced data would leave the
results reported here unchanged, and would have to be measured again under imbalance and
under federation before the deployment reading could be extended to it.}

ops.rationale: Splits the 335-word paragraph into the foundation-model arm, the task definition and the federated simulation, states the upsampling result as a possible gain of 0.013, replaces foundation family and the software wording, cuts the repeated scope and lead clauses and two binary contrasts, and adds the flutter and pooled-scaling limitations.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The foundation-model arm is limited in its input rate and in the models it holds.
ECGFounder expects 500\,Hz input, and because the 500\,Hz release could not be obtained in
full for this study, the main benchmark embeds the 100\,Hz cohort upsampled to the expected
length. A comparison on a 300-record subset gave ECGFounder an ARI of 0.909 with the
upsampled 100\,Hz input and 0.896 with the native 500\,Hz input. The upsampled input may
therefore raise ECGFounder's ARI by about 0.013 on that subset, which is small against its
$k$-means lead of 0.242 over the hand-crafted features. We evaluate two foundation models.
Other foundation models, including some reported to cluster well \cite{lookingbeyond2026},
are not included, and Section~\ref{sec:discussion} sets out how this bounds the
conclusions. The MIT-BIH arm has no foundation-model row, for the lead reason given in
Section~\ref{sec:methods}.}

\rev{Both evaluated tasks are binary by design, one rhythm contrast and one morphology
contrast, each chosen so that the class definition is unambiguous and a clustering failure
can be charged to the representation rather than to label noise. No multi-class arrhythmia
cohort is evaluated, and no result here is a statement about multi-class arrhythmia
structure, where several rhythms share an irregularity signature and the largest class
outnumbers every minority. A multi-class PTB-XL rhythm cohort over the same embeddings is
the least costly way to test whether the ordering survives that setting. The AF class also
includes atrial flutter, which can conduct with a regular ventricular rhythm, so the
flutter records among the AF positives may not fit the reading that SR and AF differ in
rhythm regularity.}

\rev{The federated study simulates ten sites within one dataset. Its only control on
heterogeneity is the Dirichlet concentration, which moves class prevalence across sites
and nothing else, and the spread that alone produces is already wide: over the ten redrawn
non-IID partitions ECGFounder ranges from chance to 0.881, while the hand-crafted features
stay between 0.455 and 0.643. Feature scaling in the simulation is fitted on statistics
pooled over all sites, which a real federation would not have, and
Section~\ref{sec:results} shows that feature scaling changes the results by a wide margin.
Device vendor, lead placement, population case mix and local labelling practice also differ
between hospitals and are absent from the simulation. Settling their effect needs ECG
records held at several institutions, clustered under a federated protocol with the site
of origin retained as a variable, which was not available for this study.}

ops.rationale: Replaces the representation-not-algorithm shape with the spread comparison it rests on, keeps the full scope statement here, names the conv-AE, restricts all five clusterers to PTB-XL, uses feature scaling, cuts the restating clause and keeps the open questions as a sentence of their own, without semicolons.
ops.new_text:
\rev{For unsupervised arrhythmia structure in the ECG, the spread of ARI across
representations exceeded the spread across clustering algorithms within each
representation that clustered well, and chance-corrected external evaluation was required
to see it. This held on the two tasks evaluated here: SR-versus-AF rhythm separation in
PTB-XL and N-vs-V beat morphology in MIT-BIH. On balanced PTB-XL data ECGFounder,
pretrained on more than ten million recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}, leads. Under class
imbalance 16 interpretable hand-crafted features overtake it, and under simulated
federation across ten heterogeneous sites they are the more predictable of the two,
retaining 0.92 of their centralized ARI against 0.69 and never falling below 0.455 over the
ten site draws. On PTB-XL the raw and conv-AE pipelines sit at chance under all five
clusterers. Internal indices and feature scaling are not neutral and must be reported.
Whether these results hold for multi-class arrhythmia cohorts, for other foundation models
and for a real multi-institution federation is open.}
